provenance.scope_note: One-pass, read-only analysis of this run's disk artifacts only. Website source, backend, administration, field analytics, and prior runs were not used.

candidates.title: robots.txt advertises a sitemap URL that returned HTTP 404
candidates.observation: The captured public robots.txt names https://addp.vn/pub/sitemap.xml as its Sitemap URL. The run recorded HTTP 404 for that URL; it also recorded HTTP 404 for https://addp.vn/sitemap.xml. These are endpoint observations from this collection, not proof of persistent availability or search-engine impact.
candidates.suggested_direction: Check the publicly advertised sitemap location and publish a valid sitemap there, or update the robots.txt Sitemap directive to the intended reachable URL.
unknowns: Whether the 404 response was transient or persists beyond the run's collection time.
Whether a valid sitemap is available at another untested URL or through a sitemap index.
Whether search engines currently know or have processed another sitemap location.
Whether the sitemap response body is an application error page or another custom 404 response; only status and byte count were recorded in the indexed fact.
candidates.observed_problem: robots.txt advertises https://addp.vn/pub/sitemap.xml, and that URL returned HTTP 404 in this run. The alternate tested URL https://addp.vn/sitemap.xml also returned HTTP 404.
confirmed_external_facts: https://addp.vn/robots.txt returned HTTP 200 and its captured contents include 'Sitemap: https://addp.vn/pub/sitemap.xml'. Evidence: EVD-C51AC48D3DB98538.
probable_technical_causes: The advertised sitemap may not be published at the configured path, or the route may be misconfigured. This is a hypothesis, not a confirmed implementation cause.
developer_investigation: Verify the intended public sitemap endpoint and its response status and XML content from an external client.
Check that the robots.txt Sitemap directive points to the verified endpoint.

rubric.scope: Page instances/endpoints only: the robots.txt directive and two recorded HTTP responses are evidenced. This is not a sitewide behavior pattern claim.
Single public-file instance. HTTP 200 and captured wildcard disallow directives are observed; crawler-specific interpretation and actual bot access were not tested.
